headline: Sell New Orleans first and the Pelicans second: paid, hand-made city craft timed to king cake, second lines and crawfish.
thesis: New Orleans fans wear the city before the team: Dirty Coast and Fleurty Girl phrase tees, ward numbers and school colors beat a Pelicans logo that only dates to 2013, in a town that watched the Jazz leave and the Hornets spend two Katrina seasons in Oklahoma City. The city runs on its own clock (second-line Sundays from Labor Day to June, king cake from Jan 6 to Mardi Gras on Feb 9, 2027, crawfish from Lent through Jazz Fest), and that clock overlaps the NBA season almost exactly. After a 26-56 season, with first-year coach Jamahl Mosley and no 2026 first-round pick, standings won't sell product; craft and calendar will. Plan roughly two-thirds of units as city-first product carrying a secondary Pelicans mark and one-third as player and team product, commission the city's hands (sign painters, brass bands, bounce artists, school programs) on their terms, and drop on New Orleans dates rather than league dates.

archetype.name: The Second Line
archetype.description: They dance behind the city's main line (Saints, LSU and Carnival), loyal through two lost franchises and loud when the music is right. They buy city pride first and team gear second, and they punish anything that reads tourist.

pulse.teamMoment: New coach Jamahl Mosley inherits Zion Williamson, breakout scorer Trey Murphy III (21.5 ppg, kept through June trade rumors) and second-year Derik Queen and Jeremiah Fears after a 26-56 season and a quiet offseason under Joe Dumars. The team is not on the opening-night or Christmas slates; NBA Cup West Group B (OKC, MIN, LAC, MEM), opening Oct 30 at the Clippers, is the early-season stage.
pulse.sentiment: Weary, not angry: protective of Murphy, hopeful on Queen and Fears, cautious about building anything on Zion's availability, and more excited by the 'NOLA Nights' Skelican City Edition than by the roster.

topInsights.title: City mark first, team mark second
topInsights.insight: Locals put local phrase tees over team gear, and the Pelicans compete with Saints black-and-gold and LSU purple-and-gold for the same shirt drawer. The 2023-24 'NOLA Nights' City Edition (purple, neon green and the skeletal Skelican), brought back in 2025-26, showed that a New Orleans-after-dark story beats the standard marks.
topInsights.implication: Make every hero piece pass as New Orleans pride on the street, with the Pelicans mark as a secondary lockup, jock tag or sleeve hit, and keep a lean one-third of units team- and player-led.

topInsights.title: The NBA season is second-line season
topInsights.insight: Social Aid & Pleasure Clubs parade most Sundays from Labor Day into June in new color-matched suits and fresh sneakers, the city's living fashion show, and they keep their colors secret until parade day. No other NBA market has a weekly street-style ritual on the same calendar as its home schedule.
topInsights.implication: Build tonal, color-matchable sneaker and warm-up sets for the general line, and treat any club collaboration as the club's project: paid, credited, and released only if and when the club wants.

topInsights.title: Carnival color is tourist shorthand; the city's craft isn't
topInsights.insight: Purple, green and gold is on every souvenir in the Quarter and blurs into LSU, while the team's own fan-favorite City Edition went to purple and neon green at night instead. What locals haven't seen on a jersey is the hand-made civic city: blue-and-white tile street names, sign painters' dot-bordered lettering, iron lace and brass-band drum heads.
topInsights.implication: Use commissioned craft (tile numerals, hand-lettered alphabets, iron-lace jacquard, brushed-brass hardware) as the design system, and keep Carnival color to small January accents.

topInsights.title: Food is the most precise retail clock
topInsights.insight: Pelicans attention peaks October to December, then the city's own seasons take over: king cake from Jan 6 to Feb 9, fish fries and crawfish from Ash Wednesday (Feb 10) into May, sno-balls all summer. The team already has the season's best inside joke, the King Cake Baby.
topInsights.implication: Sequence drops by what's on the table: a king cake knit on Jan 6, a crawfish-red pack from late February, nectar-cream pink for spring and summer. Never launch a hero drop in the final two weeks before Mardi Gras.

topInsights.title: Identity is ward, school and side of the river
topInsights.insight: New Orleanians place each other by high school ('What school you went to?') and by ward, which bounce records shout out by number, while the West Bank and New Orleans East rep separately. School programs like St. Aug and Edna Karr, and HBCUs like Xavier, Dillard and Southern, carry more block-level loyalty than a losing pro team.
topInsights.implication: Build modular ward and side-of-the-river product first, drawn by artists from each area, and phase school and HBCU co-brands in through each institution's own licensing office.

topInsights.title: Permanence beats promises
topInsights.insight: Basketball has left New Orleans twice, so fans in a 26-56 season worry less about wins than about whether the team is rooted here. Murphy is the player fans trust, Zion is the most famous name (and a Jordan Brand athlete), and the brown pelican itself, back from near-zero after DDT, is a comeback story nobody has put on product.
topInsights.implication: Tell 'still here' stories (pelican in her piety liners, ward and school ties) instead of contention messaging, and lead player product with whichever young players Nike actually has relationships with.

topInsights.title: The sacred line is also the market's credibility test
topInsights.insight: Black Masking Indian suits, chants and patches are sacred and individually authored, second-line regalia belongs to its clubs, and bounce was built by queer Black artists such as Katey Red and Sissy Nobby. This city beat the NFL over the 'Who Dat' letters in 2010, and it calls out brands that borrow without paying.
topInsights.implication: Pay up front and credit by name, never print or trace Indian beadwork, and get consent from each club, band and artist directly rather than through a single gatekeeper.

opportunities.title: Twelfth Night Pack
opportunities.summary: The season's biggest city-specific drop, released Jan 6 when king cake season and Carnival begin: a navy ground with a fine sanding-sugar fleck, doubloon jock tags and, if cleared, the King Cake Baby, instead of beads, masks or block Carnival color.
where: Pelicans Team Store, Smoothie King Center
Fleurty Girl (French Quarter, Lakeside Metairie and Gretna doors)
opportunities.when: Jan 6 launch through Mardi Gras Day (Feb 9, 2027); restock by mid-January, with no new hero launch after about Jan 26
opportunities.how: Ship the pack in a king-cake-style box and give away paid Dong Phuong king cake slices at a Carnival-season home night rather than bundling cake with retail. Put the baby on a waistband tab only after the Pelicans confirm they own it and it is cleared for apparel; otherwise use a plain plastic-baby silhouette drawn fresh.
products: Sanding-sugar knit warm-up (navy ground, small fleck)
opportunities.segment: Diehard locals, families and Carnival visitors
opportunities.kpi: Sell-through of 50% on entry tees and 35% on premium knits by Feb 1, and January Pelicans revenue versus January 2026

opportunities.title: Ward Call, phased
opportunities.summary: A modular identity line of tile-set ward numerals plus West Bank and The East pieces, each drawn by a paid artist from that area, launched small and widened across the season.
opportunities.when: Phase one at the first confirmed home game after Oct 30 with three areas (7th Ward, West Bank, The East); full ward set rolls out December to February; school co-brands are a 2027-28 phase two
opportunities.how: Open with a paid, rotating bounce lineup for an arena ward-by-ward call-and-response, offered first to pioneers such as Katey Red, Sissy Nobby and DJ Jubilee, with artist credit on the hangtag and the scoreboard. Add Big Freedia only after her footwear and apparel obligations are cleared.
opportunities.segment: Neighborhood locals, West Bank and East families, and young hoopers
opportunities.kpi: Units by ward code, share sold outside Orleans Parish core doors, and repeat buyers across two or more drops

opportunities.title: Still Here holiday core
opportunities.summary: Capture the year's peak attention (November through December) with accessible city and kids product, player pieces only for names whose apparel status is confirmed, and a 'still here' piety story.
opportunities.when: Confirmed Friday Cup home nights between Oct 30 and Nov 27, Black Friday, and through Dec 24
opportunities.how: Bundle a kids swingman with a ward tee at a value price, and use one 'Friday night in New Orleans' giveaway graphic that works against any Cup opponent. Add a navy warm-up with a pelican-in-her-piety liner that explains the name; route any Zion piece through Jordan Brand.
opportunities.segment: Families, gift buyers and Gulf South regional fans
opportunities.kpi: Holiday units versus 2025, kids share of jersey sales, and city-first versus player unit mix against the two-thirds plan

opportunities.title: HBCU and school-pride nights
opportunities.summary: Ride the city's two biggest school-pride peaks: Bayou Classic weekend for HBCU fans and the LHSAA basketball playoffs for high school families, with the institutions as licensors and beneficiaries.
where: Xavier (Gert Town) and Dillard (Gentilly) campus events
opportunities.when: Bayou Classic weekend (Thanksgiving weekend, Nov 27-28, 2026, pending the Pelicans schedule) and a Friday home game in February to early March during the LHSAA playoffs
opportunities.how: Build an HBCU-coded capsule licensed through Southern's and Grambling's own programs for Classic weekend and through Xavier and Dillard for a local HBCU night. For high schools, start with one willing program or alumni association, route it through its athletic and licensing office, and make gear or gym funding the headline.
opportunities.segment: HBCU alumni and fans, high school families and Bayou Classic visitors
opportunities.kpi: Attendance and sales on HBCU and school nights, dollars returned to programs, and whether a second school asks in

opportunities.title: Brass series
opportunities.summary: Treat Pelicans Gold as sousaphone brass: foil, hardware and drum-head lettering credited to a named brass band, each drop paired with instruments for school bands.
where: Maple Leaf Bar and Tipitina's (launch events)
opportunities.when: A December home-game launch outside Classic weekend, with a second wave after Mardi Gras
opportunities.how: Lead with Rebirth Brass Band if its members' deals clear, credit the band on the product, and fund instruments through the Tipitina's Foundation or The Roots of Music. A separate, paid St. Augustine Marching 100 story can headline a home night, credited as a high school program, not an HBCU one.
opportunities.kpi: Sell-through by drop and instruments funded

opportunities.title: Second Line Sunday pilot
opportunities.summary: A first-season, no-product pilot: pay one Social Aid & Pleasure Club and its brass band to bring a second line to a Sunday home game, credited by name, and let the club decide whether product ever follows.
where: Smoothie King Center, a Sunday home game
opportunities.when: Agree terms in September and October; the arena second line runs on a Sunday home date the club chooses
opportunities.how: Get the club's written consent directly, pay the club and band, and route any parade fee support through a culture-bearer intermediary the club picks. If the club later asks for product, make a small, numbered, club-owned run on its timeline, with the swoosh kept off its regalia.
products: Club-owned numbered set only if the club asks
opportunities.segment: Second-line culture and style-led Black New Orleanians
opportunities.kpi: The club's public endorsement and whether another club asks to be next

opportunities.title: Boil Season and Nectar Cream
opportunities.summary: Give the post-Carnival stretch and summer their own palette (boiled-crawfish red, nectar-cream pink, seersucker) in heat-ready mesh, and take one activation to the city's outdoor courts.
where: Joe W. Brown Memorial Park (New Orleans East) and Behrman Park (Algiers)
opportunities.when: Late February (after Ash Wednesday, Feb 10) through Jazz Fest, then summer; avoid the March Super Sundays and St. Joseph's Night (Mar 19)
opportunities.how: Launch Boil Season around the team's actual home schedule, with a Play-In tee printed only if the team gets there. Switch to Nectar Cream with a paid sno-ball stand collab and a summer court run at Joe W. Brown or Behrman with mesh and sleeveless product, and a poster-style tee from a paid Black New Orleans artist in the Jazz Fest window, with no festival marks.
opportunities.segment: Locals in festival season, summer hoopers and spring visitors
opportunities.kpi: March-to-May Pelicans apparel revenue versus 2026 and court-event youth reach

opportunities.title: Claiborne Oaks artist capsule at Essence
opportunities.summary: An artist-owned capsule, offered as an invitation, in which a Black New Orleans painter renders the live oaks the I-10 overpass removed from Claiborne Avenue, launched to the national audience at Essence Festival.
opportunities.when: Essence Festival of Culture, July 4 weekend 2027
opportunities.how: Invite BMike Odums or another Tremé or Seventh Ward artist, with a real option to decline; the artist owns the work, the credit and the choice of Claiborne Corridor beneficiary. Keep it off the uniform and away from Aug 29.
products: Premium hoodie with oak side panels
opportunities.segment: The national Black audience at Essence and culture-led locals
opportunities.kpi: Essence-weekend revenue, out-of-state share of buyers, and dollars returned to the corridor

collection.name: Made by Hand
collection.story: New Orleans marks its identity by hand: tiles at every street corner, sign painters' lettering, sousaphone brass, king cake sugar and the crawfish table. This collection is built with the people who make those things, credited and paid, so a Pelicans fan wears the city's own handwriting instead of a souvenir.

themes.name: Corner Tile
themes.story: Every New Orleanian knows their corner by its blue-and-white tile street name; this theme sets wards, neighborhoods and numbers in that tile grid for 2026-27 lifestyle product.
themes.graphics: Square-tile block capitals with a tile border for TREMÉ, 7TH WARD, WESTBANK and THE EAST, plus a crescent-and-star water-meter roundel as a quiet secondary mark.
themes.materials: Heavyweight cotton jersey with a glazed-look high-density print, debossed rubber crescent-and-star patches, and Dri-FIT mesh for the shooting shirts.

pieces.detail: One area per tee in tile type, drawn with a paid artist from that ward.
Short-sleeve cobalt mesh with glazed-white tile-grid numbers and a tile-border hem.
A youth cut with the neighborhood name and a hidden pelican tile.
Debossed water-meter roundel on the front, ward number on the side.

themes.name: Brass and Iron
themes.story: Pelicans Gold already reads as a tarnished sousaphone bell; this theme pairs brass-band hardware and drum-head lettering with original iron-lace patterning.
themes.segment: Music-first locals, band culture and premium buyers
themes.graphics: Circular drum-head lockups lettered by a New Orleans sign painter, and an original iron-lace railing drawing with a hidden 'NO' monogram.
themes.materials: Brushed-brass zipper pulls, aglets and snaps, laser-cut iron-lace perforations, tonal jacquard knit, and satin taping.

pieces.detail: Laser-cut lace panels at the yoke with brushed-brass hardware.
A credited brass band's name arched over a circular sign-painted lockup.
Pelicans Gold foil wordmark and a brass drawcord tip.
Tonal lace side panel with the monogram in the scrollwork.
Braid and cross-belt trim co-created with a paid, licensing band program.

themes.name: Twelfth Night
themes.story: King cake sanding sugar as a fine fleck on a navy ground, read as glitter on dark rather than flat Carnival blocks, with doubloons and, if cleared, the King Cake Baby hidden inside.
themes.graphics: A sparse sugar-crystal fleck on navy, two-sided doubloon jock tags with a new theme each season, and a small baby or doubloon on the waistband tab.
themes.materials: Navy knit with a metallic-fleck yarn at under 10% coverage, and anodized-aluminum two-sided doubloon tags.

pieces.detail: Navy body with a sparse tri-color crystal fleck and a doubloon pull.
A baby or doubloon on the waistband tab and a doubloon on the leg.
Navy tee with a printed doubloon and the season's theme.
A numbered set of Pelicans doubloons made with a local doubloon maker.

themes.name: Boil Season
themes.story: The stretch run and summer in the colors of the newspaper-covered crawfish table and the nectar-cream sno-ball, built for 80°F festival days and outdoor courts.
themes.segment: Festival-season locals, spring visitors and summer hoopers
themes.graphics: A newsprint-grain texture under crawfish red (with no real mastheads), hand-painted sno-ball-stand menu lettering, and navy-and-white seersucker stripes.
themes.materials: Perforated mesh, quick-dry woven, navy-and-white seersucker panels, and packable water-resistant shells.

pieces.detail: Perforated mesh with a newsprint-grain sleeve and navy numerals.
Open-hole mesh in boil red for summer runs at Joe W. Brown and Behrman.
Seersucker side panels on a navy mesh body.
Pink footbed, navy strap and a hand-lettered 'nectar' hit.
Navy shell with a nectar-pink lining that packs into its own pocket.

uniform.narrative: At almost every corner in the city, the street name is set in blue-and-white tile in the sidewalk, and every New Orleanian has stood on theirs. The jersey spells NEW ORLEANS tile by tile in glazed white on a cobalt body, wraps it in an original iron-lace side panel, and puts the city's hand-made civic design on court. This is a pitch for 2027-28, since the 2026-27 set is already locked; back-plan it so concept, Pelicans sign-off and NBA approval land on the league's next submission window, and run its tile and iron-lace language on 2026-27 lifestyle product in the meantime.
motifs: Square-tile block capitals set on a grid, with a tile border around the wordmark
Original iron-lace railing drawing with a hidden 'NO' monogram in the scrollwork
Pelican in her piety, the state's comeback bird, inside the collar
uniform.typography: A 'NEW ORLEANS' wordmark and numbers built square by square on a tile grid, drawn and signed by a paid New Orleans sign painter, in glazed-white fills with a thin navy outline on cobalt. No script and no fleur-de-lis in the wordmark.
details: Base: cobalt, chosen to contrast clearly with the white Association set and the navy Icon set
Waistband: ward numerals in tile type running around the band, plus WESTBANK and THE EAST
Side panel: tonal iron-lace jacquard in a deeper cobalt, with the monogram at hip height
Jock tag: debossed brass crescent-and-star roundel with the lettering artist's signature
Court: tile-bordered street-name corners at each baseline, as if the court sits on a city corner
avoid: Purple, green and gold as the lead: it is tourist shorthand, blurs into LSU, and the team's own fan-favorite purple-and-neon NOLA Nights set already owns purple
Fleur-de-lis as the hero: it reads as the Saints and as souvenir shorthand, the Pelicans mark already carries one, and its history in colonial Louisiana is a secondary reason for restraint
Black Masking Indian beadwork, plumes or chief iconography in any form, and copying any club's regalia
Katrina waterlines, FEMA X-codes, voodoo and Bourbon Street or 'N'awlins' tourist shorthand
Copying a real tiled street name, a specific building's railing, or Simon's or Dr. Bob's signature styles

alternates.name: Sousaphone
alternates.idea: Navy with brushed Pelicans Gold as brass and numbers in drum-head sign-painter lettering, co-designed with a credited brass band and paired with school instrument donations.

alternates.name: Streetcar
alternates.idea: St. Charles streetcar olive green with gold roller-sign numerals and iron-lace side panels, a quiet fall alternate.

partners.name: Dirty Coast
partners.why: Its neighborhood in-jokes are what locals wear over team gear, the city-first voice the Pelicans lack.
partners.idea: Paid co-designer of Ward Call copy and of city-only rapid-response tees with no player names or likenesses.

partners.name: Fleurty Girl
partners.type: Local tee and gift brand (French Quarter, Lakeside Metairie and Gretna doors)
partners.why: It became the local face of the city's tee vernacular when the NFL sent its 2010 'Who Dat' letters, and it reaches local women and families on both sides of the river.
partners.idea: Host the Twelfth Night drop in its doors and co-design a family and kids Carnival tee.

partners.name: Bounce artists (Katey Red, Sissy Nobby, DJ Jubilee; Big Freedia once cleared)
partners.type: Rotating paid lineup of bounce pioneers and DJs
partners.why: The ward-by-ward call-and-response is the city's most local typography, and credit belongs to the group that built it, not one headliner.
partners.idea: Paid arena sets for Ward Call launches and the Decadence-weekend night, with names on hangtags and the scoreboard.

partners.name: Xavier, Dillard, Southern and Grambling
partners.type: HBCUs and their licensing and band programs
partners.why: HBCU pride peaks on Bayou Classic weekend, and Xavier and Dillard are the city's own Black college communities.
partners.idea: Licensed HBCU-night capsule with proceeds and band support returned through each school's program.

partners.name: Studio BE (Brandan 'BMike' Odums)
partners.why: The city's most credible street artist, whose work paints back what was lost after Katrina and urban renewal.
partners.idea: An invitation, which he can decline, to own the Claiborne Oaks capsule and choose its beneficiary.

partners.name: Rebirth Brass Band with the Tipitina's Foundation
partners.type: Brass band and school music nonprofit
partners.why: Rebirth is the standard every second-line band is measured against, and the foundation equips school band programs.
partners.idea: Credit Rebirth on the first brass-series drop and fund instruments for every unit sold, once members' deals are checked.

partners.name: Dong Phuong Bakery
partners.why: Its king cake draws lines from every corner of the metro, and it carries both the Carnival and Vietnamese New Orleans stories.
partners.idea: Paid supplier of king cake for an in-arena Carnival-night giveaway and a named food partner for a Tết game-night element.

partners.name: Backstreet Cultural Museum
partners.type: Community museum of second-line and Black Masking culture, Tremé
partners.why: It knows who to ask, but it is one advisor, not a gatekeeper for every club or tribe.
partners.idea: Paid advisor on the Second Line Sunday pilot who names who else belongs at the table; consent comes from each club and band directly.

where: Taste: Dirty Coast on Magazine Street, Fleurty Girl's French Quarter, Metairie and Gretna doors, St. Claude pop-ups and Studio BE, where limited drops land first.
Volume: Lakeside (Metairie) and Oakwood (Gretna) mall doors and Dick's, where families buy kids jerseys and mainstream colorways.
Launch: the Pelicans Team Store at Smoothie King Center for Ward Call, Twelfth Night and school and HBCU nights.
Regional: a Gulf South line (ward-free 'Louisiana' and 'Gulf South' tile pieces) sold in Baton Rouge, Acadiana and Gulf Coast doors and online for fans outside the metro.
when: Late October to December is peak Pelicans attention and the year's biggest gifting window.
Jan 6 to about Jan 26 for Carnival product; no hero launch in the two weeks before Mardi Gras (Feb 9).
Bayou Classic (Thanksgiving weekend), the LHSAA playoffs (February to early March) and Essence (July 4 weekend) for school-pride and visitor drops.
Late February through Jazz Fest for the lightweight stretch-run and festival palette.
how: Plan about two-thirds of units as city-first product with a secondary Pelicans mark and one-third as player and team product.
Tier the range: value kids, tee and swingman bundles for local households, and numbered keepsake pieces for visitors, with separate sell-through targets per tier.
Design for 60-80°F parade days and air-conditioned arenas: mesh, seersucker, packable shells and color-matchable tonal sets.
Pay and credit every collaborator up front and send money back visibly (instruments, school programs, corridor groups), because this market checks.

risks.risk: Cultural extraction, such as anything resembling Black Masking Indian beadwork or an unpaid second-line reference, would end Nike's credibility with the communities that set the city's style.
risks.mitigation: Keep sacred material out of every brief, pay culture bearers up front, and get written consent from each club, band and artist directly.

risks.risk: Player product depends on deals Nike may not hold: Zion is a Jordan Brand athlete with a long injury history, and Murphy, Queen and Fears' apparel arrangements are unconfirmed.
risks.mitigation: Confirm each player's arrangement before assigning product, run Zion pieces through Jordan Brand, and lead with city and ward product where deals are unclear.

risks.risk: Another sub-30-win season or a Murphy trade at the Feb 11 deadline could crater team-gear demand and feed fan worry about the team's permanence.
risks.mitigation: Hold team-branded volume to about a third, keep rapid-response tees city-only, and tell 'still here' stories rather than contention.

risks.risk: Third-party IP is everywhere: Saints fleur-de-lis treatments, 'Who Dat', krewe marks, HBCU and high school marks (some tied to other brands, and involving minors), the King Cake Baby, NBA and NBPA player rights, and Hornets-era marks owned by Charlotte.
risks.mitigation: Use original commissioned art, route school and HBCU work through each institution's licensing office, clear the King Cake Baby with the Pelicans, and keep local-brand tees free of player likenesses.

risks.risk: Unknown 2026-27 home dates could put launches on road nights, and hurricane season (June 1 to Nov 30) can wipe out summer and early-fall events; Aug 29 is a day of grief.
risks.mitigation: Pin every in-arena launch to a confirmed home date, keep digital fallbacks, and schedule nothing commercial around Aug 29.

scorecard.rationale: Few NBA cities have a deeper or more design-ready local culture, and its calendar lines up with the season. But retail is thin (few destination sneaker doors, a modest arena store, a price-conscious core), and Pelicans fandom is small, Saints-first and weary after 26-56. The opportunity sits just below average, held up by city-first product that can sell regardless of the standings.
